claim: When a highlighted range's end extends past the found start line, generateCodeFrame computes how many characters of a later line to underline as `end - count`, but `count` at that point marks the boundary just before the previous line's terminator, not the start of the current line's content; for CRLF sources this leaks the 2-byte terminator into the underline count, so an `end` that lands exactly at the start of a following line produces a spurious extra caret on that line where the equivalent LF source produces one fewer (verified by running the algorithm: for longSourceCrLf with end at the start of the '// 2' line, the underline is '^^' on '// 2', while the identical logical position on the LF longSource produces only '^' — contradicting the fix's own stated goal that the frame should point to the same location regardless of line endings).
reason: Traced the algorithm symbolically for the j>i branch: entering that branch count still equals the previous line's end-of-content offset (the position of its terminator), so `end - count` includes the terminator length rather than the offset into the current line, and for CRLF (terminator length 2) this adds one extra caret versus LF (terminator length 1) at the same logical position, e.g. 2 carets vs 1 caret when end lands exactly at the start of the '// 2' line in the new test's longSource, which is exactly what the pack's own new snapshot for 'works with CRLF given a range' shows ('^^' on line 5), confirming the defect is real and present in the changed code.
